topic: MicroGPT-C: 10M TPS on Apple M5 in Pure C

key_points: Primary repo behind the 10M TPS claim; char-level transformer in one dependency-free C file (libc only), forward/backprop/Adam/sampling, 4192 params, trains on ~32k names.
Benchmarks: Apple M5 Pro NEON 10,168,430 tok/sec (median 15 runs); AMD Ryzen 5 5600H AVX2 6,927,775 tok/sec; same binary under Rosetta 2 only 2,225,024 tok/sec (1/3 native, not for benchmarking).
Builds on macOS/Linux/Windows (MSYS2), ARM64 NEON + x86-64 AVX2. Train/inference use separate forward passes (gpt_forward vs gpt_forward_infer).
Generalization: trained on 20,000/32,033 names, 2.2054 nats/char on seen, 2.2039 on unseen, beats interpolated trigram with ~5x params.
docs/PERFORMANCE.md details: column-major weights, split accumulators, hoisted (token,pos) prefix table, deferred RMS scale, fused sampling, vocab padded to 4.
HN discussion (11 pts, dhorthy submit). Independent test on AMD Ryzen 9 9800x3d gave 7,647,173 tok/sec; commenter planning CUDA kernel napkin-math ~2B tok/s on a 5090.
Common critique: 'this is not an LLM' — it's a char-level name generator, not a real language model.
Suggestion that Arm SME could go faster (network could fit in the ZA register).
References earlier faster C port moebiusV/cugpt (~2500x speedup vs Python).
Earlier standalone C port of Karpathy's microgpt.py (Feb 2026), ~900 lines, explicit forward/backward + manual gradients, MIT license.
Default 500 steps on 32k names in ~0.02s (vs python 296.68s); larger config (26,816 params) trains in 2.37s. Benchmarked on Apple M1 Pro.
Shows the 'C port' genre predates the 10M-tps repo and shares the same minimal single-file premise.
Divergent fork/rework: Zero-dependency C99 GPT-2 engine 'for edge AI' with Organelle Pipeline Architecture (OPA) coordinating specialised micro-models, 114 stars, MIT, 335 commits.
Claims 91% win rates on 11 logic games with 30K-160K param models; benchmarks on Apple M2 Max. Emphasizes 'composition beats capacity' rather than raw inference speed.
Useful contrast: same project name, different thesis (orchestration vs raw throughput).
Aggregator digest of the same HN story, restates headline numbers (10.1M tps M5 Pro, 6.9M Ryzen 5 5600H, 4192 params).
Confirms the story circulated across news aggregators (brevfeed, allthenews, pulseaugur) in Aug 2026.

stats.fact: MicroGPT-C reaches 10,168,430 tokens/sec (10.1M TPS) single-threaded on an Apple M5 Pro with NEON — median of 15 runs.
AMD Ryzen 5 5600H with AVX2 hits 6,927,775 tok/sec (median of 5 runs) on the same algorithm.
The same binary under Rosetta 2 on Apple Silicon measures 2,225,024 tok/sec — about a third of native.
The model has 4,192 parameters; trains on 20,000 of 32,033 names in a couple of seconds.
Generalization: 2.2054 nats/char on training names and 2.2039 on unseen names, beating an interpolated trigram with ~5x parameters.
Roughly half the per-token time (~240 of ~500 cycles) goes to the MLP; the workload is issue-width-limited, not stall-limited.
Independent HN test on AMD Ryzen 9 9800x3d scored 7,647,173 tok/sec.
An earlier C port (moebiusV/cugpt) claims ~2500x speedup over the Python original.

angles: Context matters: 10M TPS is a 4,192-parameter char-level name generator, not an LLM — reviewers should frame the number honestly.
Apple Silicon vs x86: same algorithm, only kernels differ (NEON vs AVX2) — M5's wide 128-bit core drives the lead, not an unfair test.
The engineering is the story: column-major matvecs, split accumulators, hoisted prefix table, deferred RMS scale — how a tiny model saturates issue width.
Issue-width-limited, not wait-limited: the doc proves the machine is busy, so speedups must come from fewer instructions, not better scheduling.
Batching is the stated ceiling-raiser — turning every matvec into a matmul.
Hype vs substance: HN pushback ('not an LLM') and the real takeaway (tiny C models, C/Python camp, on-device AI).
Rosetta 2 reality check as a cautionary benchmark note.
